text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

Brazil's trade deficit in November was $853 million, below October's record $1.308 billion trade gap. Exports totalled $3.912 billion, against imports of $4.765 billion. So far this year, the country's trade deficit has amounted to $3.754 billion.
-- FUEL PRICES RISE UP TO 14 PCT
Fuel prices will rise by 14 percent, instead of between 9.0 percent and 10 percent as previously estimated.
U.S. aviation authorities certified the new 50-seat Embraer EMB-145 regional jets, allowing it to go into commercial service in the United States
-- BANCO DO BRASIL PUNISHES EMPLOYEES IMPLICATED IN PPB LIST
Federal bank Banco do Brasil has punished two employees implicated in allegations of a leaked list of members of the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB) in debt with the bank.
-- GOV'T ASKS FUNDS FOR PROJECTS FOUND IRREGULAR BY THE GENERAL ACCOUNTING OFFICE
The federal government's budget proposal for 1997 asks funds for 134 projects which were considered irregular by the General Accounting Office.
-- BANERJ'S SELLOFF POSTPONED FOLLOWING JUDGE DECISION

The Rio de Janeiro state government decided to postpone Tuesday's auction of its state bank Banerj following a court injunction granted to the Association of Banerj's Employees. Planning Secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar expects to sell the bank by December 27.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom, 55-21-5074151
